object_description: three-storey rectangular cube set orthogonally to the existing building in a green meadow
design_condition: the rectangular cube is set orthogonally to the existing building in a new green meadow, its small footprint leaving much open space while zoning a shared entrance and break area

positive: The added three-storey volume zones a common entrance and break area with the existing building
The small footprint leaves a lot of open space
The school is accessible from north and south via a very attractive, spacious arcade
The main entrance is central and opens to the common break area
The new building is airy and light with a wooden frame structure
The design deliberately sets itself apart from the massive existing structure
Large-format wooden metal windows and horizontal fibre cement parapet bands characterise the facade
Fabric awnings ensure sun protection
Wooden ribbed ceilings and wood-based panels dominate the interior
A warm workshop atmosphere can be expected from the materials
The extra-high ground floor holds all rooms needing quick access from the old building
Auditorium, library, staff and housekeeping are grouped around the central access space
The auditorium can be enlarged by opening folding walls
The exposed teachers room gives a very good overview of the break area
An additional open lounge area is offered on the north side
Amorphous wardrobe furniture cushions the linear rigour of the floor plan
The upper floor lounge area has direct daylight and openable windows
The building is accessible by lift in addition to the stairs
The green flat roof can also be used as an energy harvesting area
Bracing via the lift core, shear-resistant ceilings and diagonal struts removes most walls
Rooms can therefore be expanded or opened into open-plan areas
The compact building shape and the low share of usable space aid profitability
A very attractive project that promises scope, with uses accommodatable differently
negative: The crown of the protected tree comes very close to the south-east corner of the new facade
A weather-protected connection to the old building is missing
The storage space would be better placed in the middle zone for direct auditorium access
There are no general event toilets on the entrance floor
The division of workshop, machine space and storage is bad, though improvable
The circulation areas are kept very limited and are not suitable for multiple use
The comparatively large floor areas and building volumes are cost-driving
Architectural adjustments such as moving the stairs back are possible but not in the project
A connecting piece for covered access to the old building is imaginable but not proposed
These and further inadequacies add up into the negative
